title: New York Stop Hiding Hate Act
summary: Large social media companies operating in New York must publish their terms of service and report to the NY Attorney General twice a year on how those terms deal with hate speech and racism, extremism and radicalisation, disinformation and misinformation, harassment, and foreign political interference.
applies_to: Social media companies operating in New York with more than $100 million in gross annual revenue.

key_dates.event: Reporting starts; companies file twice a year

requirements: Publish the terms of service in accessible language, with a contact for questions.
Describe how users can report violations and how the company may respond.
Report whether the terms define each category, and how moderation addresses it, including automated systems and human review.
Report the number of posts flagged and actioned (removal, demonetisation, deprioritisation).
penalties: Up to $15,000 per violation per day after a 30-day notice period.
what_you_can_do: Read each platform's filed reports to see its current rules and how it responds to user reports.
If a platform does not handle reports according to its published rules, contact the NY Attorney General's office using the complaint form.
status_note: X Corp. is challenging parts of the law (X Corp. v. James, S.D.N.Y. No. 1:25-cv-05068). The court has paused enforcement of the definitions and enforcement-data provisions against X while the case is pending, so X's filings omit them.
